title: Landfall and Current
premise: Lior Brightwater, a desert ranger who has spent years outrunning her family's disgraced name, tracks a thief named Sable Vane across the salt flats to the drowned coast, where the monsoon season traps them both. The tide reveals a sea cave holding the Tideheart, an artifact that grants command over water and memory, and Lior learns Sable stole it not for profit but to keep it from the corrupt Harbor Council who weaponized it against their own people. As the storm floods the coast, Lior must choose between returning to invisibility or standing with Sable and the found family of salvagers sheltering in the cave; she ends by shattering the Tideheart, freeing its stolen memories back to the townsfolk, and accepting that staying—being seen—is worth the cost.
about_author: Jude Halloran is the pen name of a former marine salvage diver turned novelist who grew up in coastal fishing towns before moving inland to write. Their work blends hard-edged adventure with quiet meditations on belonging, and Landfall and Current is their third novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stopping
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She picks up the trail of a thief who robbed a caravan shrine, tracking across the salt flats with grim efficiency. Flashbacks reveal why she left home: her father's name ruined by the Harbor Council. Emotional beat: restlessness as armor—she keeps moving because stopping means remembering.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She corners the thief at the drowned coast but loses him in the tide flats as the first storm clouds gather. A dying fisherman warns her about the cave that 'opens twice a year and takes payment.' Beat: frustration curdling into unease as the land itself turns hostile.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Sable's POV introduced. He hides the stolen artifact—a dull stone called the Tideheart—in the sea cave just as the tide recedes, revealing its entrance. He knows Lior followed him. Beat: guilt and resolve; he stole it to protect people, not rob them.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She enters the cave at low tide and finds Sable waiting, unarmed, offering truth instead of a fight: the Tideheart holds memories the Council extracted from citizens to control them. Beat: reluctant alliance born of shared enemies.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Storm signals force both to abandon the flats; Sable's leaking boat can't make open water, and Lior's ranger skills can't fix rot. They strike a bargain: help each other survive until the season breaks. Beat: wary cooperation over a failing fire.

chapters.title: The Salvagers of Greywater Cove
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Lior's eyes. They reach a cove settlement of scavengers led by old Brannoc, who recognizes the Tideheart and shelters them without questions. Beat: warmth Lior doesn't trust—found family offered by strangers feels like a trap.

chapters.title: Leaks
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Repairing the boat, he confesses his sister was one of the memory-harvested, left hollow by the Council's collectors. Lior shares her own exile. Beat: two guarded people trading wounds like currency.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She discovers Brannoc keeps records of everyone the Council erased—including, impossibly, her mother's name. The Tideheart hums when she touches it, showing fragments. Beat: hunger for memory versus fear of what it will cost.

chapters.title: Riders on the Flood
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A Council patrol boat hunts the coast during the storm's eye, forcing the cove to hide the strangers. First skirmish; a young salvager, Wren, is nearly taken. Beat: the enemy becomes real, and so does the stakes of staying.

chapters.title: Payment Due
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The cave 'takes admission': prolonged contact with the Tideheart erodes the holder's own memories. Lior realizes her mother may be alive inside it—or what's left of her. Beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The salvager girl idolizes Lior and asks to be taught tracking. Lior refuses, then relents, teaching her to read weather instead. Beat: Lior discovering she has something to give, not just something to flee.

chapters.title: The Council's Collector
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The collector who hollowed his sister arrives under truce flags, offering amnesty for the Tideheart—and names Lior Brightwater as a wanted fugitive, turning the cove's goodwill uncertain. Beat: betrayal's shadow over fragile trust.

chapters.title: Divided Water
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Brannoc wavers; some salvagers want the reward. Lior prepares to leave alone, repeating her oldest habit, but Wren stops her at the shore. Beat: the cost of stopping made visible—and survivable.

chapters.title: Storm Surge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The monsoon hits full force; the cove floods, the boat is destroyed, and retreat is impossible. Everyone shelters in the sea cave together. Beat: catastrophe stripping away pretense—there is no leaving now.

chapters.title: Inside the Heart
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Trapped with the artifact, she dives deep into its memories and finds her mother's voice, and the truth: her father was destroyed for trying to expose the harvests. Beat: rage transmuted—the exile was never her shame.

chapters.title: The Collector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Collector's POV. He offers Lior her mother's memories restored in exchange for the Tideheart intact, knowing the Council will rearm it. Sable begs her to refuse. Beat: temptation wearing the face of love.

chapters.title: What Memory Owes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She almost accepts, then understands the memories belong to everyone harvested, not to the Council's ledger. She refuses. The collector calls the patrol. Beat: resolve hardened by grief—some prices are worth paying.

chapters.title: Cave War
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Patrol forces storm the cave at high tide. Brannoc, Wren, and the salvagers fight beside Lior and Sable; Brannoc falls buying time. Beat: found family proven in blood—the invisible woman is no longer fighting alone.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cornered at the Tideheart's altar, she chooses to shatter it rather than let it be reclaimed. The stored memories flood out as light and rain, returning to their owners across the coast. Beat: climax—destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: Aftercurrent
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The storm breaks. People across the cove wake remembering stolen years; Sable's sister surfaces from her haze calling his name. Beat: exhausted, trembling hope.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With the Council exposed and leaderless, survivors begin rebuilding. Lior buries Brannoc and formally takes Wren as an apprentice. Beat: mourning braided with belonging.

chapters.title: Staying
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Offered a ranger's commission restoring lawful order to the coast, she accepts—not to run, but to remain. She visits the sealed cave one last time and leaves her father's compass there. Final beat: stillness chosen freely; the current carries her forward without carrying her away.
